question: Explain the scope of 'supply' under section 7 of the CGST Act, 2017. Which activities are treated as supply even when made without consideration?
sources: CGST Act, 2017 - section 7 scope of supply
CGST Act, 2017 - Schedule I, Schedule II and Schedule III

points.label: Supply for consideration
points.description: All forms of supply of goods or services, such as sale, transfer, barter, exchange, licence, rental, lease or disposal, made or agreed to be made for consideration in the course or furtherance of business.

points.label: Clubs and associations; import of services
points.description: Activities of a person other than an individual for its members for consideration are supply; so is import of services for consideration, whether or not in the course of business.

points.label: Without consideration: business assets
points.description: Permanent transfer or disposal of business assets on which input tax credit has been availed is a supply even without consideration.

points.label: Without consideration: related or distinct persons
points.description: Supplies between related persons or between distinct persons (such as branches in different States) in the course of business are supply even without consideration.

points.label: Without consideration: agents and imports
points.description: Supply of goods between a principal and an agent who supplies or receives them on the principal's behalf, and import of services from a related person or own establishment outside India in the course of business, are also covered.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, Schedule I, paras 3 and 4

points.label: Activities that are not supply
points.description: Activities in Schedule III, such as services by an employee to the employer in the course of employment and services of courts, are neither supply of goods nor services; Schedule II decides whether an activity is goods or services.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, section 7(2) and (1A); Schedules II and III
